claims.text: What the strip looks like ST elevation in the lateral leads (I, aVL, V5–6) with reciprocal ST depression in the inferior leads (III and aVF).
claims.quote: ST elevation in the lateral leads (I, aVL, V5-6). Reciprocal ST depression in the inferior leads (III and aVF).
claims.locator: How to recognise a lateral STEMI

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) ST elevation: I, aVL, V5, V6; reciprocal depression in II, III, aVF; likely LCx or diagonal
claims.quote: Lateral I, aVL, V5, V6 II, III, aVF LCx or diagonal

claims.text: High lateral STEMI: ST elevation mainly in I and aVL
claims.quote: ST elevation primarily localised to leads I and aVL is referred to as a high lateral STEMI.
claims.locator: How to recognise a lateral STEMI

claims.text: Reciprocal inferior change appears only with ST elevation in I and aVL, and concomitant inferior ST elevation (inferolateral STEMI) may cancel it
claims.quote: Reciprocal change in the inferior leads is only seen when there is ST elevation in leads I and aVL. This reciprocal change may be obliterated when there is concomitant inferior ST elevation (i.e an inferolateral STEMI)
claims.locator: How to recognise a lateral STEMI

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Arteries: branches of the LAD and LCx supply the lateral wall
claims.quote: The lateral wall of the LV is supplied by branches of the left anterior descending (LAD) and left circumflex (LCx) arteries.

claims.text: Patterns: anterolateral (LAD occlusion); inferior-posterior-lateral (LCx occlusion); isolated lateral (D1, OM or ramus intermedius)
claims.quote: Three broad categories of lateral infarction: Anterolateral STEMI due to LAD occlusion. Inferior-posterior-lateral STEMI due to LCx occlusion. Isolated lateral infarction due to occlusion of smaller branch arteries such as the D1, OM or ramus intermedius.

claims.text: Usually part of a larger infarct, e.g., anterolateral STEMI
claims.quote: Infarction of the lateral wall usually occurs as part of a larger territory infarction, e.g. anterolateral STEMI.

claims.text: Lateral extension of an anterior, inferior or posterior MI means more myocardium at risk and a worse prognosis
claims.quote: Lateral extension of an anterior, inferior or posterior MI indicates a larger territory of myocardium at risk with consequent worse prognosis.

claims.text: Treatment A stand-alone indication for emergent reperfusion
claims.quote: Lateral STEMI is a stand-alone indication for emergent reperfusion.
